### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/automation.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/automation.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fdb92db00b3380bb166e749f377960c42db0831` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9899cc1aa567e370ead60d1d8cbbda2ff9cc4b8c` — the merge of head `817bde9da3402971acdb908eca09f6a7960565a2` into base `3fdb92db00b3380bb166e749f377960c42db0831`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9899cc1aa567e370ead60d1d8cbbda2ff9cc4b8c && git checkout 9899cc1aa567e370ead60d1d8cbbda2ff9cc4b8c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3fdb92db00b3380bb166e749f377960c42db0831 817bde9da3402971acdb908eca09f6a7960565a2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3fdb92db00b3380bb166e749f377960c42db0831 && git merge --no-ff 817bde9da3402971acdb908eca09f6a7960565a2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fdb92db00b3380bb166e749f377960c42db0831
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3fdb92db00b3380bb166e749f377960c42db0831` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `817bde9da3402971acdb908eca09f6a7960565a2`
Local-runs: none

Read, and nothing else: card #19939's stage plan `6096263424` (S3's row and its family finding), the S1 and S2 landing records `6101473453` / `6109915858`, S2's contract review FAIL `6109203893` and its order `6109208049`, this stage's claim `6110982937`, the dev's reports `6112804256` and `6114354985`, the seat's sync order `6112829060` and the ACCEPT `6114388191` (read for what they assert, not adopted); PR #22883's body and the net diff `git diff 45e206e498 817bde9da3` (merge base with `origin/main`; 87 files, +1389 / −445, equal to the PR's file list, 26 non-test, 61 test); ADR-0032 Decisions 2 and 3, the contract table and Sequencing 6, ADR-0087 D2 and D3, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`CATEGORIES`, `breakingDeclaration`), `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (the pre-mode exemption) and `.changeset/pre.json`, all on `origin/main` `63739521d8`; the hop `3e6eedc786..817bde9da3`; the head's check-runs, polled from 2026-10-11T22:10Z until every run had a conclusion. Read-only throughout: no worktree, no build, no test, no gate re-run; `python3 -I` parsed the API JSON and `git` read the refs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set.** `LoopConfigSchema.collection` goes from `z.union([z.string().min(1), z.array(z.unknown())])` with `xExpression: 'template'` to `FlowCollectionSlotSchema`; `MapConfigSchema.collection` from `z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.unknown())])` to the same. `FlowCollectionSlotSchema` (`builtin-node-config.zod.ts`, imported into `control-flow.zod.ts`) is `z.union([z.array(z.unknown()), AssignmentExpressionValueSchema])`: a list, or a CEL value envelope. A string is refused, every string: the union's `error` hands a non-envelope input to `collectionLiteralRefusal`, which gives a `{…}` token the value-slot judge's own refusal (`valueSlotTemplateRefusals(value, { collection: true })`, word for word) and a bare name the rule plus the envelope naming it (`{ dialect: 'cel', source: celPath(name) }`); a malformed envelope leads with `VALUE_ENVELOPE_REFUSAL`. The three doors are the same parse: `registerFlow` and `objectstack validate` through `flowNodeConfigRefusals` (the contract map parses `map` always and `loop` only with a `body`, `parsedWhen`), the executor through `parseNodeConfig` against the same schemas. At the base an envelope at either key failed the union with zod's default message, verified by reading the base contract. RIGHT (ADR-0032 Decision 2: a computed value is whole-field CEL; Decision 3: the single brace deleted; Sequencing 6; the stage plan's S3 row and family finding).
- **The legacy loop.** `loop-node.ts`'s body-less branch is byte-unchanged: it reads `raw.collection` as a bare name into `$loopItems` / `$loopIndex` and parses nothing. The ledger's new `onlyWithKey: 'body'` on the `loop collection` row is read by `readOn` (`config[key] != null`) in both walks, which is the contract map's `parsedWhen` (`config.body != null`) spelled in the ledger; `flow-node-expression-paths.test.ts` holds the two equal over configs with and without a body, and pins that no other entry carries the field. RIGHT.
- **No other position moved.** The ledger diff moves exactly the two `collection` rows (`flow-template` → `value`, plus `onlyWithKey` on `loop`); `resolveFlowNodeExpressions`' simplification (`entry.role === 'predicate'` dropped from two guards) is equivalent once the role union is `'predicate' | 'value'`; `valueSlotTemplateRefusals` branches only under `options.collection === true`; `guardOf` gains a defaulted parameter; the `judge` closure's boolean became an options object with every caller migrated to the same value; `FlowValueSlotSchema` and the callee and screen slots are untouched; `atOrInsideJudgedLedgerSlot` changes a comment only. `api-surface/automation.json` adds three names and removes none. RIGHT.
- **The judge.** `COLLECTION_SLOTS` keys the two ledger entries; `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals` judges a collection before the callee and screen arms with `{ collection: true }`, so only the value itself is read: an inline array's strings are data (the executors never interpolated one). `collectionRemedy` names the envelope for a whole path and a guard answering `[]` (`has(vars.rows) ? vars.rows : []`), never the value slots' `null` guard, since `null` fails the node; any other token "never computed a list". The build doors' value arm refuses a token-free string in the contract's words (`flow-builtin-node-config-values.test.ts`), a token is left to the judge, as before. Pinned both ways (`flow-value-slot-template.test.ts`: the contract and the judge use the same words). RIGHT.
- **The executors.** `resolveCollectionSlot` (`value-slot-map.ts`) is `isExpressionEnvelopeShaped(value) ? engine.evaluateValueEnvelope(value, variables, 'collection', context) : value`: an envelope is evaluated in the run's scope; an inline array is returned as written and never reaches `interpolate`. `loop` (structured) and `map` call it and fail the node with `collectionNotAList`, which names what the envelope evaluated to and its source. The token arm, the bare-name arm and the `variables.get` fallback are deleted from both executors; `interpolate` is no longer imported by either. No `??` was added. The 21 engine pins (`collection-value-slots.test.ts`) cover both positions: refused at `registerFlow` and at the executor's parse; an envelope iterates, a computed one too; an inline array iterates as written; absent → `EXECUTION_ERROR` "Unknown variable: rows"; `[]` guard iterates nothing; `null` and a string → `NODE_FAILURE` naming the kind and the source; the legacy loop unchanged. RIGHT.
- **Readers left that interpret a string collection.** In the executors, none: the structured `loop` and `map` parse first and a string never reaches the resolver. Two readers remain outside them, each by design: (i) the legacy body-less `loop`, which reads a bare name and is judged nowhere (the contract and the stage plan both keep it); (ii) the lint's `validate-flow-template-paths.ts`, whose `collectionListText` reads an envelope's `source` and falls back to `loneTokenBody` (a lone `{…}` token or a bare name) for a source written before this change, only to infer the iterator's object and keep that rule's findings on a flow every door now refuses. It runs nothing and evaluates nothing, so it is not a PD #12 dialect fallback; S7's resolver deletion can take the fallback with the residual calls. Acceptable, named here so it is not mistaken for a surviving arm.
- **The retired role and the ratchet.** `'flow-template'` leaves `FlowNodeExpressionRole`; the ratchet's `ROLE_BY_MARKER` (`config-expression-ledger.test.ts`) drops `template`, and a new pin walks every descriptor and schemaless JSON Schema and asserts no slot carries that marker, so a `'template'` marker fails `roleOf` as unknown. The `loop` and `map` descriptors carry `xExpression: 'value'` on `collection`; the contract carries no marker, so `map.collection` is declared on one channel (pinned). At the head no non-test source carries `xExpression: 'template'` (one stale docblock, below). True and in scope: the role recorded these two slots and nothing else, and the stage that empties it is the one to retire it.
- **The lint's collection reader.** `validate-flow-template-paths.ts` infers a loop iterator's object from an envelope naming a variable, as it did from the token; without it every migrated loop's `{iterator.field}` path checks would have gone silent. Pinned (an envelope resolves; a computed source is silent). The `@objectstack/lint` `patch` is right for a fix with no authoring surface. True and in scope.
- **The reach.** Shipped sites migrated in this diff: `examples/app-showcase` (`showcase_batch_reminders` and `showcase_nested_fan_out_reminders` loops, `showcase_release_signoff` map), `examples/app-todo` (`task_reminder`, `overdue_escalation`) — five, each a whole `{name}` token on a structured node; `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` (three samples, the value-slot list, a new paragraph, the legacy-loop sentence); `packages/services/service-automation/README.md` (`:191` row, `:211` paragraph, the sample). Spot-checked with `git grep` at the head over `examples`, `packages/platform-objects`, `packages/qa/dogfood`, `content/docs`, `apps`, `skills` and the README: 0 string-valued `collection:` (two prose mentions of the refused bare name); the same grep at the merge base reads 9, the positive control. The generated references (`control-flow.mdx`, `builtin-node-config.mdx`, `index.mdx`) describe the new union. No shipped flow is newly refused. `.objectui-sha` does not move (`4997995022`), so `Console Pin Gate`'s skip is expected; the local objectui checkout (`2a48bd408d`) has no non-test import of `LoopConfig` / `MapConfig`, so the pinned console keeps building; the designer's `collection` pickers and `FlowNodeInspector.loopItemVariable-9340.test.tsx` are the seat's objectui companion, as the plan assigns. hotcrm is NOT MEASURED here (no clone); the dev's reading (eleven structured loops on spec 17.7.0) goes on the seat ledger, the plan's carrier. RIGHT.
- **The sync hop** `3e6eedc786` → `817bde9da3`: three commits — `f7ee0386ed` (merge of `origin/main` `40bc51f3f9`), `8f0446c6e8` (one path, `content/docs/references/index.mdx`, regenerated), `817bde9da3` (merge of `origin/main` `45e206e498`). 114 hop paths; 112 byte-identical to `main` at `45e206e498`; the two that differ are the two hop paths this PR also touches, `index.mdx` and `packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.test.ts`, and on each the PR's own hunk is identical before and after the hop (`index.mdx` differs only by the schema count main moved, 1520 → 1522). 85 of the 87 PR files are blob-equal across the hop. No PR source moved. `main` has since gained 4 commits (to `63739521d8`) touching none of the PR's 87 paths; GitHub reads `mergeable: true`. RIGHT.
- **Out of the claim's file surface**, each declared in the PR and each the class the claim admits: the lint reader and its test; comment-only edits (`validate-expressions.ts`, `flow-node-config-refusals.ts`, `flow-text-slot-template.ts`, `schemaless-node-config.zod.ts`, `engine.ts` incl. the `evaluateValueEnvelope` docblock S1 carried here and the registration failure header, which no longer says template slots require braces); collection fixtures in `metadata-protocol` and `lint` tests; the four generated artifacts and the references. No governed surface is in the file list. RIGHT.
- **Sentences this diff makes false and does not touch**, both internal docblocks of the class S1's PASS carried forward (S1 carried the `evaluateValueEnvelope` docblock to this stage): `packages/spec/src/automation/node-executor.zod.ts:268` — "Slots marked `xExpression: 'template'` are recorded but not checked: no validator implements the single-brace `{var}` dialect" (no slot carries the marker now and the ratchet refuses it; `:276`'s "a plain string there stays `{var}` interpolation" has been false since S1); and `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts:1455` — "A `flow-template` slot's blank is untouched". Carrier: S7 (the canon fixes), beside the `engine.ts` value-role comment and the `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment the PR already carries there. Non-blocking.
- **One site the census grep did not cover:** `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts` (tracked, ships in the package) writes `collection: '{tasks}'` / `'{rows}'` / `'{items}'` in the `flow-node-map-flow-alias` fixture's `before` and `after` (`:1375`–`:1393`) and `'{leads}'` in a loop fixture (`:15481`, `:15533`). These are D2 fixture pairs for other conversions, exercised by `conversions.test.ts` structurally (`toEqual` on `after`, a notice count), never parsed by a door, so nothing is newly refused; S1 left the same class there (`input: { caseId: '{record.id}' }` at `:1432` / `:1448`, `inputs` at `:3697` / `:3712`). Not a shipped flow. Noted for S7's canon pass. Non-blocking.

### ② Semver level

- **Packages.** `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation` are the published packages whose `src/**` moves; `@objectstack/lint` moves one source file (the reader) and one comment; `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` moves tests only; the examples are private; docs are no package. The changeset names exactly those three. RIGHT.
- **Level.** `.changeset/pre.json` on `main` is `{ mode: pre, tag: next }`, so `check-changeset-no-major` returns `exempt` on a `major`; S1 and S2 graded the same two packages `major` on this line. `major` for `spec` and `service-automation`, `patch` for `lint`: RIGHT. The `!` in the title, the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM → TO table (six rows, the `[]` guard and the legacy loop included), the one-line fix: present. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing: …; widening: …)`** — RIGHT on the value and on the arm, and judged here on the diff, not on the seat's ruling. `matchValueToken` reads `yes` (followed by a space, not `|`); `readArmToken` reads `(narrowing` as the arm, since `:` is outside the token class, so the reader returns `{ declared, yes, narrowing }`: "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read." Measured on the diff: the narrowing is a string refused at two published authoring keys; the widening is a CEL value envelope newly accepted at both (the base unions had no object arm), the published JSON Schema (`any[] | { dialect, source, … }`) and the inferred `LoopConfig['collection']` / `MapConfig['collection']` gaining that arm, and three new exports on `api-surface/automation.json` (`FlowCollectionSlot`, `FlowCollectionSlotParsed`, `FlowCollectionSlotSchema`, origin `builtin-node-config.zod.ts`). The claim's `no (narrowing)` rested on the plan's premise, which the measured diff falsified, exactly as S2's `recordId` did (`6109203893`). The line is byte-identical on both carriers (PR body line 2, changeset line 9). One precision, non-blocking: the published `FlowNodeExpressionRole` loses the `'flow-template'` member and the published `FlowNodeExpressionPath` gains an optional `onlyWithKey` — both stated in the changeset's kit, neither named in the line's parenthetical; the arm and the level already cover them.
- **ADR-0087 marker.** `not-required (already-registered flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused)`: the category is in the gate's closed vocabulary, and the id resolves at the head and existed at the base (the entry file is `M`, added by S1), which is what `already-registered` re-validates. Exactly one marker in the changeset body, which also carries the `Clause-②` line the gate reads the arm from. `check-adr-0087-registration` is the dev's exit 0 and `Check Changeset`'s green. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **D3 only, no D2 — RIGHT.** Neither spelling maps losslessly, verified on the code, not from the report: at the base `interpolate(rawCollection)` on an absent `{rows}` returned `null`, `variables.has('{rows}')` was false, and the executor returned `{ success: false, error: "… did not resolve to an array" }`, a returned failure (`NODE_FAILURE`); at the head `evaluateValueEnvelope` throws on the absent variable and the step records `EXECUTION_ERROR` "Unknown variable: rows" (pinned). A bare name: on a legacy loop it works today (the unchanged branch reads `variables.get(name)`); on a structured `loop` or `map` the base's `interpolate('rows')` was the identity, `collection == null` was false, the `variables.get` fallback never fired, and the node failed every run — so `rows` → `{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'rows' }` turns a node that never iterated into one that does. ADR-0087 D2 takes losslessly mappable changes only and sends semantic changes to D3. No `src/conversions/*` source moves (one test fixture file only).
- **The D3 amendment** of `18.flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused.ts`: the header comment, `surface` (the two collections, "any string value: a single-brace template token, or a variable's bare name"), `replacement` (the envelope, the inline array as written, the bare name as that name in an envelope, the `[]` guard), `reason` (the `NODE_FAILURE` / `EXECUTION_ERROR` difference, the bare name's semantic change, the untouched legacy loop) and `acceptanceCriteria` (decide whether the loop should run at all before rewriting a bare name). One entry per retirement family, amended, not duplicated — the S1/S2 way. `migrations/registry.ts` is gitignored and regenerated at build, so its absence from the diff is right; `STEP18_RATIONALE` in `registry.ts.template` is unchanged and carried to S7, as S1 and S2 left it. RIGHT.
- **Dev deviations (`6112804256`, `6114354985`), each answered:** the `Clause-②` line written against the claim — measured, recorded in the PR, judged right above; the `flow-template` role retired in a file the claim holds — in scope, above; the lint reader and comment-only crossings — mechanical, above; the classifier refusal of a `bash -c` gate loop re-issued as two literal commands — process, no removal involved, no finding; one misdirected command in the shared checkout that wrote nothing — process, no finding; the service-automation suite re-run at the final head in the sync round, closing round 0's gap; the index regeneration folded into `8f0446c6e8` rather than a separate commit — the hop analysis above shows one regenerated path and no source moved; `main` moving past the verified head with zero path overlap — verified above, still zero at `63739521d8`.
- **Carriers, each judged right:** #22585 for `SKILL.md:65` (`skills/**` is Tier H and names no dialect — not false); the objectui companion for the designer's pickers and the parsing test (the plan's carrier; at the pin the console builds); the seat ledger for hotcrm (NOT MEASURED, the plan's carrier); S7 for `STEP18_RATIONALE`, the `engine.ts` value-role comment, and — added by this review — `node-executor.zod.ts:268` / `:276`, `flow.zod.ts:1455`, the lint's `loneTokenBody` fallback, and the `conversions/registry.ts` fixtures. #22586 (the v18 changesets correction) still waits on the card; this changeset's "supersedes that line" sentence follows S2's accepted precedent.
